texts: good. the fullness is reified so the date attaches to it and the plain "the moon was full" fact is kept alongside; the only residue is that "day 96 of Year 1" lands in the day-of-month position of the date vocabulary, which no rewrite avoids.
good. the Council and the Watch are both typed as ordinary definite referents, and the convening carries the Council as its doer and the Watch as its place.
good. the salt-bloom season is typed and linked to season generally, and the opening carries the Council as doer with the season as what it acts on.
good. "the salt-bloom rations" is a specific group typed as salt-bloom rations, and "for the winter" is kept on the standardizing with winter as a plain season term.

bad: "exempted the Northcove from salt-bloom" is read as an origin phrase, so the parse asserts that the exempting came *from* salt-bloom — a whence relation your sentence never states — and what the Northcove was actually exempted from is recorded wrongly. Hang the "from" on an exemption noun instead of on the verb: "The Council granted the Northcove an exemption from salt-bloom."

good. the report keeps Hesper as the reporter and the Council as the addressee, the thin-harvest claim is held as reported content rather than asserted as fact, and the thread harvest itself is still typed so later sentences can refer to it.

mixed: the distilling, the frost weeks and the "because" link to the thin harvest all come through, but "at reduced volume" is dropped with no trace — there is no slot for a phrase saying to what extent an action was carried out — so the parse records plain unqualified distilling. Make the reduced volume the object so it survives: "Cauldron Hall distilled a reduced volume during the frost weeks, because the thread harvest was thin."
good. the prediction stays sealed as something Hesper said rather than asserted as fact, with the forward shift of "would yield", the hedged "about eight vessels" and the cold months all carried.
